case_title.quote: N PARAMESWARAN UNNI v. G KANNAN AND ANOTHER
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment's heading.

number_of_accused.reason: Only one accused, the first respondent, is tried and decided.

accused_gender.quote: statutory notice under proviso (b) of Section 138 ofN.I. Act was issued to him
accused_gender.reason: The judgment uses male pronouns ('him', 'his') for the first respondent, so 'Not stated' is wrong.

accused_age.reason: No age of the accused is stated in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: No religious identity of the accused is mentioned.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community of the accused is named.

accused_occupation.reason: The accused's occupation is not described; the cheque was issued by a third person's bank drawer only.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No statement on the accused's wealth or poverty appears; the Rs 2,00,000 offer is not a wealth finding.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record is mentioned.

victim_gender.reason: The judgment never describes a victim; calling the offence 'victimless' is an inference not stated in the text.

victim_caste.reason: No victim caste or community is named.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: the first respondent/accused borrowed Rs. 64,000/- oil 13-10-1990 from the appellant/complainant
accused_victim_relationship.reason: The judgment describes a loan from the complainant to the accused, a creditor-debtor link.

offence_category.reason: Cheque dishonour under s.138 NI Act fits no listed category, so 'Other' is apt.

statutory_provisions.quote: Section 138 read with 142 of N.I. Act is attracted
statutory_provisions.reason: Only NI Act s.138 read with s.142 is charged; GCA and Evidence Act provisions are evidentiary.

weapon.reason: No weapon is involved in this cheque dishonour case.

evidence_type.quote: the first notice sent by appellant on 12-04-1991 was effective
evidence_type.reason: Evidence is documentary: cheques, bank memo, legal notices and postal endorsements.

confession.reason: No confession or admission by the accused is recorded.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: No aggravating facts are noted in the judgment.

mitigating_circumstances.quote: first respondent was willing to pay Rs. 2,00,000/-
mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating facts are noted; the offer was a settlement, not a mitigating finding.

trial_court_outcome.quote: convicted and sentenced the first respondent to undergo simple imprisonment of three months
trial_court_outcome.reason: Matches the trial court's conviction and three-month sentence.

high_court_outcome.quote: High Court allowed the criminal revision of the first respondent by setting aside the concurrent judgments
high_court_outcome.reason: Revision allowed and concurrent conviction set aside, as stated.

final_outcome.quote: we set aside the impugned judgment of the High Court
final_outcome.reason: Conviction restored with sentence changed to payment in lieu, fitting conviction_modified.

offence_finally_established.quote: Section 138 read with 142 of N.I. Act is attracted
offence_finally_established.reason: Offence under s.138 r/w s.142 stands; sentence replaced by payment in lieu.

imprisonment_type.quote: deposit the said amount of Rs. 2,00,000/-
imprisonment_type.reason: No imprisonment is finally imposed; the three-month term applies only on default.

imprisonment_years.reason: No final fixed-term sentence stands, so null is correct.

fine_rs.quote: Rs. 2,00,000/-(Rupees two lakhs only) in lieu of suffering simple imprisonment
fine_rs.reason: The Rs 2,00,000 is a payment in lieu of imprisonment, not a fine, so null fits.

neutral_facts.reason: Neutral, no names or pronouns, stops before proceedings and reveals no outcome; facts match the judgment.

offence_severity.quote: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque
offence_severity.reason: Matches the maximum punishment quoted from s.138; no minimum is stated.

attempt_completion.reason: The offence of dishonour was completed upon return of the cheques.

physical_harm.reason: No injury or death; only financial loss is involved.

number_of_offences.quote: Section 138 read with 142 of N.I. Act is attracted
number_of_offences.reason: One charged section (s.138 r/w s.142), with one conviction upheld.

financial_property_loss.quote: first respondent failed to return the borrowed amount Rs. 64,000/-
financial_property_loss.reason: The Rs 64,000 loan underlying the cheques is the stated loss.

premeditation_planning.reason: No premeditation or planning is discussed.

motive.quote: according to the appellant, first respondent failed to return the borrowed amount
motive.reason: Non-repayment is the alleged motive, marked as the appellant's allegation.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the first notice sent by appellant on 12-04-1991 was effective and notice was deemed to have been served
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Accepted evidence matches the cheques, bank memo and first notice held deemed served.

witness_credibility.reason: The court made no assessment of witness credibility.

post_offence_conduct.reason: No post-offence conduct is recorded beyond non-service, which the court did not characterise.

bail_history.quote: bail granted to the first respondent shall stand cancelled
bail_history.reason: Only the bail cancellation on non-deposit is mentioned, as the value states.

trial_duration.reason: Trial judgment, High Court and Supreme Court dates are listed as the judgment gives them.

legal_representation.quote: C. K. Sasi, Manu Krishnan G., Abraham Mathews (for P. V. Dinesh), Advs. for the Respondents
legal_representation.reason: Counsel for respondents and appellant match the judgment's listing.

investigation_status.quote: On 23.05.1991 appellant lodged a private complaint
investigation_status.reason: Private complaint lodged and trial completed; no police investigation is mentioned.

procedural_irregularity.reason: No procedural lapse is noted by the court.

appeal_history.quote: dismissed the appeal by upholding and confirming the judgment of the Trial Court
appeal_history.reason: Outcomes at each level match the judgment's account.

prosecution_argument.quote: the complaint, was filed within the stipulated time contemplated under Clause (b) of Section 142
prosecution_argument.reason: Appellant's position is inferred from the court's reasoning rather than recorded as argument; the wording overstates it.

defence_argument.quote: learned counsel for first respondent ... submitted that first respondent was willing to pay Rs. 2,00,000/-
defence_argument.reason: Matches the High Court ground and counsel's Rs 2,00,000 offer.

legal_principle_applied.quote: once notice is sent by registered post by correctly addressing to the drawer of the cheque, the service of notice is deemed to have been effected
legal_principle_applied.reason: Covers deemed service under s.27 GCA and s.114 Evidence Act, rebuttable, and reminder notices.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Jagdish Singh v. Natthu Singh, (1992) 1 SCC 647; State of M.P. v. Hiralal, (1996) 7 SCC 523
precedent_relied_upon.reason: All four cited precedents and citations match the judgment.

sentencing_rationale.quote: in view of the undertaking given by the learned counsel, we direct the first respondent to deposit
sentencing_rationale.reason: Rationale is the counsel's undertaking, with no separate reasoning, as stated.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: The court weighed no mitigating factors itself.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The court weighed no aggravating factors itself.

other_sentence_order.quote: Rs.1,30,000/-( one lakh thirty thousand) shall be paid to the appellant as compensation
other_sentence_order.reason: Deposit, compensation split and default consequence all match the judgment's directions.
